hpi_details: A 28-year-old woman presents with amenorrhea, spotting, an adnexal mass, and a beta-hCG level of 1500.
ideas: is concerned about an ectopic pregnancy
concerns: She is worried that something is severely wrong with her reproductive organs and that she might never be able to carry a pregnancy in the future.
expectations: She hopes to get an immediate ultrasound to check whether she is pregnant and find out where the bleeding is coming from.
social_hx: Non-smoker; avoids alcohol and recreational drugs

available_results.value: 2.2 cm unruptured right tubal adnexal mass with yolk sac, no fetal cardiac activity, and no significant free fluid

clinical_knowledge.topic: Unruptured ectopic pregnancy evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Unruptured ectopic pregnancy is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Plan for Unruptured Ectopic Pregnancy: Methotrexate injection if stable and meet criteria, close follow-up, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: amenorrhea, spotting, adnexal mass, beta-hCG 1500
Key HPI features: A 28-year-old female presents with amenorrhea, spotting, an adnexal mass, and beta-hCG of 1500.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Unruptured Ectopic Pregnancy.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Unruptured ectopic pregnancy.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Intrauterine pregnancy (early) without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Any signs of hemodynamic instability would indicate rupture and surgical emergency.
management_principles: Plan for Unruptured Ectopic Pregnancy: Methotrexate injection if stable and meet criteria, close follow-up
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

teaching.one_liner: Patient with amenorrhea, spotting, an adnexal mass, and beta-hCG of 1500.
red_flags: Any signs of hemodynamic instability would indicate rupture and surgical emergency

must_ask.say: When was your last menstrual period?
Can you describe the spotting: how much is there and what color is it?

must_ask.objective: Screen for pain and hemodynamic symptoms
must_ask.say: Do you have any abdominal pain, dizziness, or shoulder pain?

must_ask.objective: Ask about desire for future fertility
must_ask.say: Are you hoping to have children in the future? This affects our treatment choice.
If you're stable and meet criteria, we can treat this with a methotrexate injection instead of surgery, with close hCG follow-up.

history.answer: My period hasn't come for about six weeks, and over the past two days I have noticed some light spotting.
My cycles usually come every twenty-eight days and are very regular, but this time my period never arrived.
It is just a little bit of brownish spotting on a panty liner. There are no large clots or heavy flow.
The light spotting started two days ago and has been on and off since then.
My last regular period was about six and a half weeks ago, so I am about two weeks late.
No, I have never had spotting between my cycles or any bleeding after intercourse before this.
No, I have not felt lightheaded, dizzy, short of breath, or unusually weak.
I have had a mild, dull ache on the lower right side of my belly since yesterday, but it feels like mild cramps.
No, I do not have severe sharp pain, shoulder pain, or pain when using the bathroom.
No, I have not had any breakouts, unusual facial hair growth, or unexpected weight gain.
No, I tolerate temperature changes normally and haven't had any racing heartbeats or neck swelling.
No, I haven't noticed any fluid leaking from my breasts, and I have not had headaches or vision trouble.
My weight has been stable, and I haven't been doing extreme workouts or strict dieting.
No, I don't bruise easily, and my gums or nose do not bleed.
I am not taking any birth control pills, hormone treatments, blood thinners, or psychiatric medications.
I am sexually active with my husband. We stopped using condoms a few months ago because we are hoping to get pregnant.
I have never been pregnant before, and we really hope to have children in the near future.
I had a routine Pap smear last year and the doctor told me the result was completely normal.
I took a home urine pregnancy test four days ago after missing my period, and it came back positive.

I'm really terrified that this bleeding means something is damaged inside me and I won't be able to have children. I was hoping you could do an ultrasound today to tell me if I'm having a miscarriage or what's going on.
I do not have any chronic medical problems like high blood pressure or diabetes.
I have never had any surgeries and I have never been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter painkillers, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to medications, foods, or anything else.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I do not drink alcohol at all, and I have never used recreational drugs.
I work as an office administrator, and I live with my husband in an apartment.
There is no family history of early menopause, uterine cancer, or blood clotting disorders.
